prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single perfect site that combines beginner-friendly plain English, open-source on-chain numbers, and a habit of publishing its own losses — but the best practical approach is a small stack:

- Coin Bureau — excellent plain-English explainers (articles + long YouTube videos) that show real numbers and metrics in a way beginners can follow. Good for learning concepts and how things work.
- Dune Analytics (and Dune dashboards) — community-built dashboards that show the actual on-chain numbers behind protocols. Use Dune to verify claims, see TVL, flows, and losses from hacks/withdrawals in raw data.
- The Defiant — crypto journalism that reports hacks, protocol losses, and investigations in accessible language; good for seeing concrete examples of where money was lost and why.
- Glassnode / Nansen / IntoTheBlock — if you want polished on-chain analytics and charts. They’re more data-focused but help you see “real numbers” for markets and projects.
- Zapper / Zerion (or an openly tracked public portfolio) — if you want to follow someone who publishes their P&L, these portfolio tools let users publicly display wallets and realized/unrealized gains/losses.

Why this stack: no single “beginner education site” tends to publish its own investment losses (most educators avoid that). So combine a plain-English teacher (Coin Bureau, Bankless, or Andreas Antonopoulos for fundamentals) with transparent data sources (Dune/Glassnode/Nansen) and investigative reporting (The Defiant/CoinDesk) to see actual numbers and documented losses.

If you want, tell me:
- whether you prefer video or text,
- whether you want to track protocols or individual investors,
and I’ll give a more tailored 1–2 site/creator picks plus a couple of Dune dashboards or public portfolios to follow.
